Subject: Node footprint for APAC pilot (Helix)

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — Helix liked the latency profile and the routing fallbacks. We're moving fast and want to lock a scoped dedicated footprint in APAC for a pilot in Q4. Key asks:

- Region: Singapore (single AZ initially)
- Target peak QPS for the pilot: ~3k requests/minute (text-gen, average request ~120 tokens)
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms token-response (end-to-end)
- Data need: logs + KV cache retention 14 days, no cross-region data replication for now
- Contract ask: 6-month initial commitment with option to convert to annual

Can you send a sizing recommendation (nodes / GPU spec / burst buffer) and a rough monthly commit estimate? Procurement will want a short SOW and an outline of rolling bursts and overflow to hosted.

Attaching our internal traffic spike summary (small sample).

Best,
Amit Shah
Head of ML Infrastructure
Helix AI

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Node footprint for APAC pilot (Helix)

Amit — thanks, this is helpful. Looping in Karthik (capacity/pricing) and Lauren (commercial) so we can give a complete proposal. A few quick clarifying questions before we finalize sizing:

1) Workload mix: is the 3k QPS mostly single-turn text generation, or do you have a 10–15% multi-turn chat component that keeps KV cache hot?
2) Peak shape: how long are the spikes (minutes vs hours) and how many spikes/day?
3) Tolerance for burst routing: do you want overflow to Redwood-hosted at a hard cap, or prefer graded fallback (hosted -> eu -> us)?

Prelim thought from the demo: for p95~220ms with 120-token avg requests and the stated QPS, you should expect a baseline of 5–7 dense A100-80GB equivalent GPU workers for sustained traffic and a 2–3 node burst band for short spikes. We can shave cost further with prefix/KV caching and quantized model variants for batchy background ops.

Karthik — could you convert the above into a concrete node-by-node commit & monthly estimate and attach a short capacity workbook?

Amit — once we align on burst behavior and spike cadence we can put together the SOW draft and draft SLA.

— Chloe
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Node footprint for APAC pilot (Helix)

Amit / team — ran a quick sizing calc and attached a workbook (capacity_estimate_apac.xlsx). Highlights / assumptions in-line:

- Traffic model: 3k rpm = 50 rps sustained; assume 20% peak-factor = 60 rps peak sustained, with 4x short spikes to 240 rps for ~10 minutes (based on your sample).
- Model perf assumptions: 120 tokens / request, throughput per A100-80GB equiv = ~25 rps (real-world, fp16 + kv cache cold-hit 60%); with warm KV cache this goes up to ~55 rps for streaming-friendly models.

Sizing recommendation (pilot):
- Baseline pool: 6x A100-80GB equiv nodes (sustained handling: ~330 rps warm-cache, or ~150 rps cold-cache).
- Short-burst band: 3x additional nodes on standby (auto-burst), target to absorb 10–15 minute spikes.
- Reserve/backstop: Redwood-hosted overflow lane configured as a hard fallback for excess beyond burst capacity; prefer to route to APAC-hosted dedicated first, then hosted.

Operational knobs we recommend enabling:
- KV prefix caching (14-day retention as requested) to reduce per-token compute by ~20–40% depending on hit-rate.
- Batching window tuning: minimize latency impact by adaptive micro-batching (25–50ms windows).
- Pre-warm policy: keep half the burst band in a ready state (warm kv/cached model) to reduce cold-start latency.

Cost/commit note: 6-month reserved for 9 nodes (6 baseline + 3 burst standby) with a 20% commit discount vs on-demand hosted; workbook has monthly estimate in tab 'CommitEstimate'.

Attachments: capacity_estimate_apac.xlsx

— Karthik
Director, Solution Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Amit — quick commercial summary to align expectations before we put the SOW together:

- Contract construct: 6-month committed capacity agreement converting to monthly billed committed units on the first of the month. Overage billed at 1.25x committed unit rate.
- Commitment sizing: 9 effective nodes (6 baseline, 3 burst standby). We will map to GPU-hours in the SOW.
- SLA: 99.5% availability on dedicated pool; agreed p95 latency targets in an appendix. If we fail targets for more than two consecutive weeks, crediting logic applies (SLA credit table will be appended).
- Discounting: we can offer a stepped discount if Helix converts to annual before month 5 (details in the attached SOW draft).

Procurement next steps: please send the contact info for your procurement lead and any PO/skipping-DocuSign constraints. Once we have that, we will produce a short SOW and a redline-friendly term sheet.

CC'ing Ben for renew/expansion cadence planning.

— Lauren

2) For the 14-day KV retention: can you confirm retention will be within the APAC cluster and logs exported to our S3 in Singapore on a daily cadence?
3) We need a one-page network topology sketch for our network/security team showing egress ports and VPC peering expectations.
